nodes.description: Proposed link between the biochemical defect and symptoms: without a CBG-bound store, free glucocorticoid is normal at rest but rises less during stress, so tissues including the brain are under-exposed when demand is highest. The evidence is from Cbg knockout mice. Human data are limited to single patients and point both ways, and loss of the store alone would not be expected to lower the free rise (see the hypothesis record), so this node and the edges entering and leaving it are a hypothesis, not an established mechanism.

nodes.description: The normal function of CBG is to bind one molecule of cortisol (or progesterone) with nanomolar affinity in a surface pocket formed by residues Ala18, Ser19, Val22, Gln232, Thr240, Phe242, Arg260, Ile263, Asn264, Ser267, Phe366, His368 and Trp371 of the mature protein (the 13 residues within 4 angstroms of cortisol in both PDB 2VDY and 4C49, computed for this entry). CBG has the serpin fold but does not inhibit proteases. Its reactive centre loop is a substrate for neutrophil elastase, and loop cleavage or partial loop insertion into beta-sheet A lowers steroid affinity through helix D. Binding-defective alleles remove or weaken this high-affinity site in the secreted protein.

nodes.description: Proposed alternative link to symptoms. CBG releases cortisol where its reactive centre loop is cleaved by neutrophil elastase, and has been proposed to direct cortisol to particular tissues such as inflamed sites, liver and brain. If so, loss of CBG would lower local cortisol exposure without changing circulating free cortisol. The release mechanism is established in vitro; a resulting tissue deficit in people with CBG deficiency has not been measured.

nodes.description: Stop and frameshift alleles that end translation in or shortly after the 22-residue signal-peptide region, so that no CBG polypeptide is produced from the allele. Three are reported: p.Trp11Ter (CBG null, also called Adelaide), p.Leu5CysfsTer26 (Santiago) and p.Val55GlyfsTer44 (Montevideo). The first two stop within the signal peptide; Montevideo shifts the frame at codon 55 and terminates at codon 98. Heterozygotes have about half the normal plasma CBG, and homozygotes for p.Trp11Ter have none. Transcript levels have not been measured for any of the three.

nodes.description: Missense alleles whose product binds cortisol normally, or was not tested for binding, but is poorly produced or secreted by cells. A51V (p.Ala73Val), I48N (p.Ile70Asn) and P246Q (p.Pro268Gln) belong here. All three residues are fully buried in the crystal structures (relative side-chain accessibility 0.00 to 0.03 in PDB 2VDY chain A, computed for this entry). Ile48 and Ala51 lie on helix B and pack against the hinge of the reactive centre loop where it inserts into beta-sheet A, the region called the shutter in other serpins. In a global alignment with alpha-1-antitrypsin (44% identity) they correspond to antitrypsin Ile57 and Ala60, on the same helix as the antitrypsin retention alleles Siiyama (Ser53Phe) and Mmalton (Phe52 deletion). A folding defect with retention in the hepatocyte is therefore the likely mechanism, but intracellular retention or polymer formation has not been shown for CBG itself.

genetic_context.description: Loss of secreted protein from the allele; the secreted fraction of A51V retains normal steroid binding.

nodes.description: Missense alleles whose product is secreted but binds cortisol with reduced affinity or not at all. Residue numbers in this literature, and in the crystal structures, count from the first residue of the mature protein; the precursor (HGVS) number is 22 higher. Distances below were computed for this entry from PDB 2VDY chain A (cleaved human CBG with cortisol). Two alleles change residues that touch the steroid: W371S (p.Trp393Ser, Athens; 3.6 angstroms from cortisol) and R260L (p.Arg282Leu; 3.9 angstroms), and both abolish binding. D367N (p.Asp389Asn, Lyon) replaces a buried aspartate (accessibility 0.02) 5.0 angstroms from the steroid that contacts Phe369, Thr370, Trp371 and Asn238, on the strand that carries the pocket residues Phe366, His368 and Trp371. G237V (p.Gly259Val) lies 10 angstroms from the steroid, next to the glycosylated Asn238 whose glycan is needed for binding. L93H (p.Leu115His, Leuven) and H89Y (p.His111Tyr) lie on helix D, 13 angstroms from the steroid; Leu93 contacts Phe369 and Thr370 of the same pocket-bearing strand. In the normal protein the helix D region couples the reactive centre loop to the binding site, and that contact is a possible route for these two alleles, but how either lowers binding has not been shown. E102G (p.Glu124Gly) is surface-exposed and 18 angstroms away; why it lowers binding capacity is unexplained.

genetic_context.description: Ranges from partial loss (Leuven, about 3-fold lower affinity) to complete loss of steroid binding (G237V, W371S, R260L).

nodes.description: Asp367 of the mature protein is buried (relative accessibility 0.02) and 5.0 angstroms from cortisol in PDB 2VDY. Its carboxylate sits among Phe94, Asn238, Phe369, Thr370, Trp371 and Ser372, on the strand that carries the pocket residues Phe366, His368 and Trp371. Replacing the charged group with an amide is expected to loosen this strand. Reports of the size of the defect differ: about 4-fold lower affinity in the original report, no measurable binding in a later report from the same group, and almost no binding with increased heat sensitivity in an independent study in human 293 cells. gnomAD v4.1: allele frequency 0.036% overall and 0.7% in Ashkenazi Jewish samples. ClinVar classifications conflict.

evidence.reference_title: Novel human corticosteroid-binding globulin variant with low cortisol-binding affinity.

nodes.description: Trp371 of the mature protein is one of the 13 residues in direct contact with the steroid (3.6 angstroms from cortisol in PDB 2VDY chain A). Replacing the indole with a serine hydroxyl removes a wall of the pocket. Found in trans with CBG Lyon in the index patient, who had no plasma cortisol-binding activity. The source report gives the change as c.1282G>C; c.1178G>C is the same change counted from the start codon of Ensembl transcript ENST00000341584 (codon 393, TGG to TCG).

evidence.reference_title: Familial corticosteroid-binding globulin deficiency due to a novel null mutation: association with fatigue and relative hypotension.

nodes.description: Leu93 of the mature protein lies on helix D, 13 angstroms from the bound steroid, and contacts His89, His91, Phe369 and Thr370. It lowers affinity about 3-fold by speeding dissociation. The residue does not touch the steroid, and the route by which it acts is not established. It is the most common function-altering allele in Europeans: gnomAD v4.1 allele frequency 0.25% overall, with 3 homozygotes. ClinVar classifications conflict.

evidence.reference_title: Decreased cortisol-binding affinity of transcortin Leuven is associated with an amino acid substitution at residue-93.

evidence.reference_title: Transcortin Leuven: a variant of human corticosteroid-binding globulin with decreased cortisol-binding affinity.

nodes.description: Glu102 of the mature protein is surface-exposed and 18 angstroms from the steroid in PDB 2VDY. The structural reason for the low binding capacity is not known. gnomAD v4.1: allele frequency 0.05% in East Asian samples.

evidence.reference_title: High frequency of SERPINA6 polymorphisms that reduce plasma corticosteroid-binding globulin activity in Chinese subjects.

nodes.description: Gly237 of the mature protein is 10 angstroms from the steroid and immediately precedes Asn238, whose N-glycan is required for steroid binding and whose side chain contacts Asp367. A valine here is expected to shift the two strands that form part of the pocket. gnomAD v4.1: 12 alleles, 9 of them South Asian.

evidence.reference_title: Novel corticosteroid-binding globulin variant that lacks steroid binding activity.
evidence.snippet: This results in a p.Gly237Val substitution that is predicted to influence the positioning of two β-sheets that constitute part of the CBG steroid-binding site.

nodes.description: Arg260 of the mature protein contacts the steroid directly (3.9 angstroms from cortisol in PDB 2VDY, 3.2 angstroms from progesterone in 4BB2) and lies next to Asp23. Identified from sequence databases and tested as recombinant protein; no affected family has been described. The source names only the protein change; c.845G>T is the single-base change that produces it in Ensembl transcript ENST00000341584 (codon 282, CGG to CTG).

evidence.reference_title: Naturally occurring mutations of human corticosteroid-binding globulin.
